issues.body:
The final assertion of `test_docs_quality_runs_this_suite_unconditionally` is dead code:

    self.assertNotRegex(call_sites[0], r"^        (?:if|continue-on-error):")

`re.search` without `re.MULTILINE` anchors `^` at the start of the string only. `call_sites[0]` is a step block that always begins with `      - name: ...` (6 spaces), so an 8-space-indented `if:` / `continue-on-error:` line can never match at offset 0. The assertion passes unconditionally regardless of the step's content.

Verified empirically against the checked-in docs-quality.yml: I extracted the single call site with the test's own step-splitting regex, injected `        if: github.event_name == 'push'` directly after the `- name:` line, and re-ran the pattern. `re.search(pattern, guarded)` -> False (assertion still passes); `re.search(pattern, guarded, re.MULTILINE)` -> True (would correctly fail).

Impact: the test's other two assertions do catch outright deletion of the step, but the property the test is named for — that the parity gate runs unconditionally — is not enforced. Someone could add `continue-on-error: true` (parity drift becomes non-blocking) or `if: false` (never runs) to this step and the suite stays green. That is precisely the silent-neutering failure mode this PR exists to prevent, so the misleading name is worse than having no assertion.
issues.fix_hint:
Add re.MULTILINE to the guard and make it a real mutation test. E.g.:

    GUARD = re.compile(r"^\s+(?:if|continue-on-error)\s*:", re.MULTILINE)
    ...
    self.assertNotRegex(call_sites[0], GUARD)

(Prefer `\s+` over a literal 8 spaces so a re-indent doesn't silently re-vacuum the check.) Then prove it is non-vacuous by adding a mutation case in the same style as test_alarm_drift_fails — inject `        continue-on-error: true` (and separately an `if:`) into the step text and assert the guard now matches. Consider also asserting the enclosing job carries no `if:`, since a job-level guard would skip the step just as effectively and is not covered today.
issues.title: Vacuous assertion: the `unconditionally` guard in test_docs_quality_runs_this_suite_unconditionally can never fire (missing re.MULTILINE)

issues.body:
The buildfarm resolves its set as `ARCHIVE_FEATURES="${BUILDFARM_FEATURES:-approx-ann,filtered-ann,vec-predicate}"` (line 65). The new parity test extracts and compares only the hard-coded *default* literal via `_BUILDFARM_FEATURES`. A run invoked with `BUILDFARM_FEATURES=...` set in the environment therefore exercises a different test population than ci.yml's archive while the parity gate stays green.

The override predates this PR, so this is not a regression. It becomes worth flagging now because the PR's new comments assert that the gate keeps 'every consumer of the nextest archive opt-in feature set synchronized' and that the EC2 build farm 'must exercise that exact same test population' — which is true of the default path but not of an overridden run. The result file already records `features_b`, so the divergence is at least observable after the fact.
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) narrow the claim in the header comment and in test_archive_feature_parity.py's module docstring to say the gate pins the buildfarm DEFAULT, with the override an explicit opt-out; or (b) make the override self-announcing — emit a loud `::: WARNING: BUILDFARM_FEATURES override active, feature-state-B parity with ci.yml is NOT guaranteed` when it differs from the default, so a non-canonical PASS is never mistaken for a canonical one. Option (a) is the cheaper honesty fix.
issues.title: BUILDFARM_FEATURES runtime override escapes the parity guarantee the new gate advertises

issues.body:
The diff rewrites the line-25 header comment to `cargo test --workspace --features "${ARCHIVE_FEATURES}" (CI archive opt-in set)`, but the actual commands at lines 188-190 use the unquoted form `--features ${ARCHIVE_FEATURES}`. The documentation and the code it documents now disagree on quoting.

Behaviourally this is currently harmless — the value is a comma-separated list with no spaces or glob characters, so word-splitting produces a single token either way — and test_each_surface_executes_with_its_declared_value pins the unquoted form for build/clippy/test. But the comment is the thing a reader copies, and it no longer matches. The reformat also collapsed the previously aligned `cargo test  --workspace` spacing in that comment block relative to its neighbours.
issues.fix_hint: Make them agree — preferably by quoting the three real invocations (`--features "${ARCHIVE_FEATURES}"`, matching what ci.yml and heavy-set-alarm.yml now do) and updating the test regexes at the same time, so all four surfaces use one idiom. Failing that, drop the quotes from the line-25 comment.
issues.title: Header comment shows quoted "${ARCHIVE_FEATURES}" but the executed lines are unquoted

issues.body:
`_YAML_FEATURES = r"^\s+ARCHIVE_FEATURES:\s*([^#\n]+?)\s*$"` scans raw file text with no YAML awareness. Today it finds exactly one match per file (verified: ci.yml:403 and heavy-set-alarm.yml:109 — the neighbouring comments at ci.yml:512 and heavy-set-alarm.yml:92,107 mention ARCHIVE_FEATURES but not followed by a colon, so they do not match). That is a narrow margin: a future comment line such as `# ARCHIVE_FEATURES: see below` would be counted as a second declaration and raise `ValueError: expected exactly one archive feature declaration, found 2`.

This fails in the safe direction — loud, not silent — so it is only a maintenance nit, not a correctness problem. Worth noting because the failure message would point at a 'duplicate declaration' that is actually a comment, which is a confusing diagnosis.
issues.fix_hint: Either strip comment lines before matching (drop lines whose first non-space character is `#`), or parse with `yaml.safe_load` and read `jobs.build-archive.env.ARCHIVE_FEATURES` / the step env directly — the latter also removes the indentation- and quoting-normalisation logic that test_yaml_indentation_quoting_and_order_are_not_semantic currently has to compensate for. If the stdlib-only constraint rules out PyYAML, the comment-stripping variant is sufficient.
issues.title: _YAML_FEATURES matches on raw text, so incidental comment text can trip the uniqueness check

verdict.summary:
The core refactor is correct. ci.yml declares ARCHIVE_FEATURES at job level (verified via yaml.safe_load that it lands on jobs.build-archive.env, so it reaches both the `nextest archive` and `--doc` steps); heavy-set-alarm.yml declares it on the measurement step; `bash -n scripts/ec2-buildfarm.sh` passes; all 7 tests pass. The three drift-mutation cases (test_alarm_drift_fails, test_buildfarm_drift_fails, test_yaml_indentation_quoting_and_order_are_not_semantic) are genuinely non-vacuous — I confirmed each `.replace()` actually mutates its source rather than silently no-opping, so the gate really does red on drift in either consumer. Consumer migration is complete: no unmigrated `approx-ann,filtered-ann,vec-predicate` literal remains in any .yml or .sh outside the three canonical declaration sites.

One test-validity defect blocks approval. test_docs_quality_runs_this_suite_unconditionally's final assertion — assertNotRegex(call_sites[0], r"^        (?:if|continue-on-error):") — omits re.MULTILINE, so `^` anchors only at the start of the step string, which begins with `      - name:` (6 spaces). An 8-space `if:` can never match at offset 0, making the assertion dead code. Verified empirically: injecting `if: github.event_name == 'push'` into the extracted step leaves the assertion passing, while the identical pattern with re.MULTILINE correctly matches. The test's name promises the gate runs unconditionally, but only outright deletion is caught — neutering it via `continue-on-error: true` or `if: false` sails through. In a PR whose whole value is a gate that cannot silently stop enforcing, that is a real hole and false assurance.

Remaining items are minor/nit: a BUILDFARM_FEATURES runtime override escapes the advertised parity guarantee, a doc/code quoting inconsistency in the ec2-buildfarm.sh header comment, and a regex that fails loudly (safe direction) on incidental comment text.
